candidates.location_hint: The persistent status region that swaps its text content based on the loading state
candidates.why: Swapping entire content inside a polite live region with atomicity enabled can sometimes cause screen readers to read the whole block repeatedly or miss updates depending on the browser implementation.

candidates.location_hint: The decorative spinner element paired with adjacent text in the loading state
candidates.why: Hiding an animated graphic while leaving the text visible is standard, but some assistive technologies may still announce the hidden element's role or interfere with the live region's announcement timing.

candidates.location_hint: The transaction list items containing only payee and amount spans
candidates.why: List items currently rely solely on visual layout to convey meaning, so it is worth verifying that the structure alone provides sufficient context for screen reader users without additional labels.

candidates.location_hint: The initial mount scenario where the component first renders in a loading state
candidates.why: Mounting a live region that already contains its initial message in the same render commit is a known edge case where screen readers may fail to announce the content.

candidates.location_hint: The error region's color styling for conveying failure state
candidates.why: While the text has a role and message, relying on a specific red hue to visually signal an error condition should be verified against background colors to ensure it meets minimum contrast ratios.

candidates.location_hint: The explicit list role applied to the custom-styled transaction container
candidates.why: Forcing a list role on a visually customized container is a workaround for certain browsers, but it should be checked to ensure it does not conflict with the visual presentation or cause unexpected announcement behavior.

candidates.location_hint: The focus indicator styling for the retry control
candidates.why: The visible focus ring uses a solid outline and offset, so it is worth verifying that the contrast between the outline color and both the button background and any underlying page content remains sufficient.
